analyst_view.overall: Galatasaray are 18th of 36 with 6 points and Aston Villa 6th with 9, so both have plenty at stake: Okan Buruk's side want to move into the top 24 at home, Villa want a top-8 place. Galatasaray's long injury list (Victor Osimhen after knee surgery, Rafael Leão on a rehab programme in Doha, Roland Sallai with a back-muscle strain and Ismail Jakobs with a groin strain) is now in the numbers, which take about a fifth off their goals for it, so I no longer trim goals myself. Galatasaray beat Samsunspor 2-1 on Saturday with Uğurcan Çakır back in goal and no new injuries; Davinson Sánchez (shoulder) trained and may return. Villa drew 0-0 with Sunderland on Saturday despite 72% of the ball and have one point from their last three league games; Matty Cash (concussion), Matteo Ruggeri and Amadou Onana are out and counted, while Wan-Bissaka and Manzambi played. No referee is named yet; I keep only a small trim on shots, which the numbers do not adjust for Galatasaray's missing forwards.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals (1.1 Galatasaray, 2.0 Villa), and they now count Osimhen, Leão and Sallai out (about -20% on Galatasaray's goals) plus Jakobs and Cash at the back. My earlier view trimmed goals for those same absences, so cutting again would count them twice; with Galatasaray still scoring (2-1 v Samsunspor) and Villa blunt in a 0-0 with Sunderland, I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already counting Galatasaray's recent rise in corners won (+3%) and Villa's dip (-3.7%). Villa had long spells of possession against Sunderland and will push wide, while Galatasaray lose some width without Leão and Sallai; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, split evenly, with Galatasaray's quieter recent card count (-2.7%) already taken off. RAMS Park is loud and hostile, but that is part of the home record the numbers use, Bardakcı's ban is domestic only, and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.8 shots (13.1 Galatasaray, 13.7 Villa). They take the missing forwards off Galatasaray's goals but not off their shots, and without Osimhen, Leão and Sallai they lose their main shot-takers, with young Deniz Gül leading the line; I trim a little, to about 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, already counting Villa's sharper recent finishing (+3.3%) and Galatasaray's quieter spell (-1.9%). Galatasaray's missing forwards matter most for shot quality, which the numbers count only in goals, so I lean slightly lower, to about 9.9.
